# R325 — free one-token dense and vocabulary-head kernel audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)

## Finding

On the pinned W source, the normal free one-token verifier reaches per-projection quantized matrix-vector work (native_mmvq, when the selected tensor has a loaded native dense override) and a separate output-head GEMV. The large vocabulary head is a compelling shape to measure, but the closed B570 decode report does not attribute time to that head or to individual dense calls. The closest head microfixture is a B70 result on a different model. It cannot justify a B570 dispatch change.

Best candidate after Main's active run closes: a small, explicitly gated RPG work-group row-count comparison for the actual N=1 native MMVQ head and selected dense shapes, preserving each row's existing arithmetic/reduction order. The present native Xe MMVQ row kernel fixes RPG=8; the benchmark should compare this with a smaller row group under the actual B570, actual GGUF types and shapes. This is a diagnostic candidate, not a recommended default. First record the selected output.weight type from the closed model loader/route evidence; the IQ4_XS example below applies only if type 23 is actually selected. Do not turn on direct Level Zero submission or a new queue as a proxy for improving the GEMV.

## Run and source path

The shared closed decode report is bench/results/2026-10-12-decode-criticalpath-native-dequant-batch/README.md, W baseline source 0691bcdf, Arc B570 10 GiB and Ryzen 5600X, free LLVM 7.1.1, 32,768 prompt tokens + 16 output tokens, G16, cache 144 slots, five CPU workers. It reports 124.09 ms/token diagnostic timing, including 50.27 ms GPU-reach wait and 55.16 ms per-layer host time; those are inclusive/nested timing spans, not per-kernel costs. Decode GPU stage lines are absent in the closed R272 interpretation. The README states the native dequant batch did not change decode computation, so its prefill A/B does not identify or time this path. It is not a clean, selected-head kernel measurement.

For the task-specified --serve, MTP off, batch 0, PCIe fraction 0, segmented verifier 1 case, the verifier's T=1 head route is in src/core/verify.cpp:1202–1253. If a NativeHead loaded successfully, the final mixer runs first and then quantizes its FP32 vector to Q8_1 and dispatches native_mmvq for ncols=T at 1243–1247; greedy sampling and optional non-finite scan follow. The native head loader (src/core/native_head.cpp:25–88) validates output.weight shape/type against the supplied GGUF and uploads it, but the closed decode report/selected-tuning file does not report the actual head GGUF tensor type. Therefore the exact selected type-specific native MMVQ implementation is not established by the permitted closed result summary. In this verifier path, even type 13 reaches native_quantize_q8_1 then native_mmvq. NativeHead::run (native_head.cpp:91–108) has a separate type-13 native_q5_k_f32 shortcut for its non-verifier caller; it is not the serve verifier dispatch described here.

The model source fixes n_embd=2560 and vocabulary size 248,320 (include/strata/plan/plan.hpp and src/kernels/xe/verify_kernels.cpp sampler comments); output is a 2560→248320 vector product, one input row, with 248,320 logits. The head's exact packed weight bytes depend on its loaded GGUF type; do not infer them from the IQ3_S pack label. As a useful conditional example, an IQ4_XS/type-23 head has 337,715,200 packed weight bytes (337.72 MB decimal) by the native-MMVQ row-size formula. If it were type 14/Q6_K the formula gives 521,472,000 bytes; if type 21/IQ3_S it gives the IQ row bytes instead. These are conditional shape calculations, not observed loaded-head sizes.

For regular native dense projections, src/core/layer.cpp:145–162 quantizes the single FP32 input to Q8_1 unless an immediately preceding projection has already produced the same scratch image, then calls native_mmvq(..., ncols=1). The verifier likewise submits native matrix-vector calls at src/core/verify.cpp:679–714, 803–817, 894–895. Native-dense loading only attaches supported matrices in the GDN/QSA dense path (src/core/native_dense.cpp:131–285); format and per-layer actual route still come from the runtime's loaded GGUF/manifest. The source contains a historical timing comment for a dense_pass experiment: 302 GEMVs, 1.377 GiB weight extent, 11.64 ms GEMV time plus a separate approximate 5.9 ms data-floor estimate (src/core/layer.cpp:911–916). This comment is not a current W B570 decode measurement, has no selected-format/per-projection join, and cannot be used as the current critical-path fraction.

## Exact N=1 kernel mapping in source

src/kernels/xe/native_mmvq.cpp:587–607 selects the row-per-subgroup layout when steps <= 10, where steps = ceil((n_in / format_block_elems) / (32 / format_trait_T)). launch_row uses one 32-lane subgroup per output row and eight rows per work-group (RPG=8, lines 539–584, 597–600); the subgroup loads/decodes the row blocks and applies its Q8_1 activation, then reduces with the existing warp XOR tree. For a conditional IQ4_XS/type-23, n_in=2560, there are 10 256-element blocks/row, T=8, and steps=ceil(10/4)=3, so this N=1 shape reaches launch_row<...,NCOLS=1,RPG=8>, not the 4-warp small-K fallback. It is 31,040 groups for 248,320 rows. Q8_1 activation storage is 10×36=360 bytes; the input is 2,560 FP32 values (10,240 bytes) read by the quantizer, and output is 248,320 FP32 logits (993,280 bytes). Type-23 logical packed head weights are 337,715,200 bytes. All are formula-derived for this conditional route, not a runtime capture.

Dense shapes with larger input-block counts can instead select the 128-lane/four-warp path; dispatch depends jointly on native format traits, n_in and n_out. Exact per-layer output dimensions, native tensor types, and calls are not enumerated by the closed decode report. A single generic M=1 GEMV attribution would therefore conceal distinct dispatches.

## Existing closest measurement and its limits

The archived bench/results/2026-09-30-xe-mmvq-speed/README.md is a useful matched microfixture for one conditional output-head shape: IQ4_XS, (n_in,n_out)=(2560,248320), ncols=1, 337.72 MB weights. It host-times back-to-back in-order-queue launches, 20 calls/loop, five loops per run, after ten warmups; it reports the median of three runs on the B70. SPIR-V DP4a version is 2,124.9 us/call (2,124.0–2,125.3), with random weight bytes and a 590 GB/s random-read bandwidth reference: 158.9 GB/s or 27% of that measured B70 reference. This is not the B570, current IQ3_S model tensor, full verifier, nor end-to-end decode. Its fixed activations and random synthetic weights do not verify the selected model's format, logits, queue graph, or cache effects. The separate Xe kernel README reports parity for small BF16 GEMV fixtures but not full model shape/head performance.

No closed matching B570 component fixture was found for the actual selected head type, the current native dense projection histogram, or the whole free one-token dense/head sequence. The one-token phase remains unmeasured at kernel granularity. This is the specific gap R325 should close once the current Main run has ended.

## Ranked candidate and validation

1. N=1 native-MMVQ row-group sweep (conditional, strongest kernel-only candidate): add an opt-in fixture-only RPG specialization for the existing subgroup-per-row kernel, compare current RPG=8 with RPG=4 for the exact current head format/shape and the repeated high-byte dense shapes reported by a closed route census. RPG changes row scheduling/group size only; preserve block visitation, format decode, per-row accumulation order and subgroup reduction so rows can remain bitwise equal. Keep any production dispatch branch disabled until a unit fixture proves bitwise logits for all compared rows and tails, the actual B570 microfixture shows a repeatable improvement, and quiet end-to-end --serve shows an independent win with unchanged token IDs/logits and lifecycle. Record each matrix's type, logical bytes, shape, dispatch, completion event, per-call samples and output comparison. If RPG=4 does not beat 8 beyond variance, keep the fixed source route. This is not a direct-submission, copy-queue or host-polling experiment.
2. Existing K/V pair kernel (lower, reachability conditional): QSA decode submits same-input K and V native GEMVs separately (verify.cpp:816–817) at identical canonical shapes 2560→512. native_mmvq_pair can join two same-type same-shape products into one launch and preserves each output row arithmetic (native_mmvq.cpp:646–672); however its dispatch supports only types 2, 6, 8, 14, 20, 23, and transformed Q6/Q8 rows (892–906), excluding several IQ families such as IQ3_S/type21. This is a safe one-launch opportunity only if the actual K/V loaded type matches and the current runtime reports them as native. It affects 12 QSA layers and about 1.4 MB per layer for IQ4_XS, so likely smaller than optimizing the vocabulary head's memory stream. Verify parity and actual type reachability first; do not extend type support as part of this audit.
3. No head-format conversion / no unfused direct Level Zero path: the head's packed weight read dominates its logical data extent; changing to a denser representation increases bytes and resident capacity needs. Removing queue safety, bypassing SYCL dispatch, or enabling direct submission without event/allocator/graph lifetime qualification is not an admitted kernel optimization.

## External implementation context

Intel lists Arc B570 at 380 GB/s graphics memory bandwidth and 203 INT8 TOPS; those are board specifications, not achieved bandwidth for this model (Intel B570 specifications: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/241676/intel-arc-b570-graphics/specifications.html). A roughly 338 MB IQ4_XS head therefore has an ideal packed-weight streaming floor of about 0.89 ms at the specification bandwidth, while the old B70 microfixture took 2.125 ms. This comparison illustrates a possible head optimization margin, not an expected B570 time: quantized decode instructions, memory transaction efficiency, launch/read overhead and real weight encoding all differ. The reviewed llama.cpp CUDA MMVQ implementation (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu) uses architecture-and-format-specific shape dispatch/prefetch; its special prefetch path is explicitly restricted to one architecture because wider-memory cards may lose when requests increase. XeStrata's own port adapts that CUDA implementation but has a different subgroup row kernel, so CUDA tiling/prefetch settings should not be copied.

A primary SGLang GH200 issue reports a one-row BF16 GEMV microbenchmark at exact 2560×4096 out_proj shape and cautions that its M=1 route must be reachable in serving; this supports testing actual dispatch reachability before importing kernel ideas, not performance transfer to Xe (SGLang issue #42085: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/42085). vLLM similarly maintains shape-specific decode implementations and explicit batching/metadata decisions; its backend choices are accelerator-specific and no matching B570 quantized vocabulary-head result was found. The relevant project comparator is vLLM's ROCm MLA single-token decode selection (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py); this is attention, not dense GEMV, so it is context only.

No build, test, GPU, model, profiler, process, Git mutation, cleanup, or source edit was performed. R265/R267/R271 are not repeated; the present focus is actual dense/head one-token kernel dispatch and its measurement gap.
